# dlasd5

> Computes the square root of the i-th eigenvalue of a positive symmetric rank-one modification of a 2-by-2 diagonal matrix.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dlasd5 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dlasd5';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dlasd5( i, D, strideD, Z, strideZ, DELTA, strideDELTA, rho, dsigma, WORK ) → Float64Array
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `i` | `integer` | Eigenvalue index (1 or 2) |
| `D` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length 2</sub> | Diagonal entries (length 2) |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | Stride length for `D` |
| `Z` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length 2</sub> | Updating vector components (length 2) |
| ↳ `strideZ` | `integer` | Stride length for `Z` |
| `DELTA` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length 2</sub> | **out** · Output array for `D[j] - sigma_i` (length 2) |
| ↳ `strideDELTA` | `integer` | Stride length for `DELTA` |
| `rho` | `number` | Scalar in the symmetric updating formula |
| `dsigma` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Single-element output array; on exit, the computed sigma_i |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ 2</sub> | **out** · Output array for `D[j] + sigma_i` (length 2) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `i`: The index of the eigenvalue to be computed. $I = 1$ or $I = 2$.
- `D`: The original eigenvalues. We assume $0 \le D(1) < D(2)$.
- `Z`: The components of the updating vector.
- `DELTA`: Contains (`D(j)` - sigma\_I) in its j-th component. The vector `DELTA` contains the information necessary to construct the eigenvectors.
- `rho`: The scalar in the symmetric updating formula.
- `dsigma`: The computed sigma\_I, the I-th updated eigenvalue.
- `WORK`: `WORK` contains (`D(j)` + sigma\_I) in its j-th component.

</details>

**Returns** `Float64Array`

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dlasd5.ndarray(
    i,
    d, strideD, offsetD,
    z, strideZ, offsetZ,
    DELTA, strideDELTA, offsetDELTA,
    rho,
    dsigma,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork
) → Float64Array
```

Compute the square root of the i-th eigenvalue of a positive symmetric rank-one modification of a 2-by-2 diagonal matrix.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `i` | `integer` | The index of the eigenvalue to be computed. |
| `d` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length 2</sub> | Diagonal entries (length 2) |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | Stride length for `d` |
| ↳ `offsetD` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `d` |
| `z` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length 2</sub> | Updating vector components (length 2) |
| ↳ `strideZ` | `integer` | Stride length for `z` |
| ↳ `offsetZ` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `z` |
| `DELTA` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length 2</sub> | **out** · Output array for `d[j] - sigma_i` (length 2) |
| ↳ `strideDELTA` | `integer` | Stride length for `DELTA` |
| ↳ `offsetDELTA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `DELTA` |
| `rho` | `number` | Scalar in the symmetric updating formula |
| `dsigma` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Single-element output array; on exit, the computed sigma_i |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length ≥ 2</sub> | **out** · Output array for `d[j] + sigma_i` (length 2) |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | Stride length for `WORK` |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `WORK` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `i`: The index of the eigenvalue to be computed. $I = 1$ or $I = 2$.
- `d`: The original eigenvalues. We assume $0 \le D(1) < D(2)$.
- `z`: The components of the updating vector.
- `DELTA`: Contains (`D(j)` - sigma\_I) in its j-th component. The vector `DELTA` contains the information necessary to construct the eigenvectors.
- `rho`: The scalar in the symmetric updating formula.
- `dsigma`: The computed sigma\_I, the I-th updated eigenvalue.
- `WORK`: `WORK` contains (`D(j)` + sigma\_I) in its j-th component.

</details>

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `dlasd5()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DLASD5`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dlasd5.f).

</section>

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import dlasd5 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dlasd5';

// Compute the square root of the first eigenvalue of diag( D )^2 + rho * Z * Z^T, with 0 <= D[0] < D[1]:
const D = new Float64Array( [ 1.0, 2.0 ] );
const Z = new Float64Array( [ 0.6, 0.8 ] );
const DELTA = new Float64Array( 2 );
const WORK = new Float64Array( 2 );
const dsigma = new Float64Array( 1 );

// Using the standard interface:
dlasd5( 1, D, 1, Z, 1, DELTA, 1, 1.0, dsigma, WORK );
console.log( dsigma[ 0 ], DELTA, WORK ); // eslint-disable-line no-console

// Using the ndarray interface (second eigenvalue):
dlasd5.ndarray( 2, D, 1, 0, Z, 1, 0, DELTA, 1, 0, 1.0, dsigma, WORK, 1, 0 );
console.log( dsigma[ 0 ], DELTA, WORK ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DLASD5`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

This subroutine computes the square root of the I-th eigenvalue of a positive symmetric rank-one modification of a 2-by-2 diagonal matrix

$\operatorname{diag}( D ) \, \operatorname{diag}( D ) + \mathrm{RHO} \, Z$ \* transpose(Z) .

The diagonal entries in the array D are assumed to satisfy

$$
0 \le D(i) < D(j) \quad\text{for}\quad i < j
$$

We also assume $\mathrm{RHO} > 0$ and that the Euclidean norm of the vector Z is one.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
